label: Reset rises after unrewarded a1 and S1-favouring belief; at D2 rises on a1->S2 rare, falls on a2->S1 rare.
terms: (phase == D1) * np.tanh(belief_lo/2) ;; (phase == GO) * np.tanh(belief_lo/2) ;; (phase == D2) * np.tanh(belief_lo/2) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 1) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 1) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 2) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (state == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 2) * (prev_reward == 1)
explanation: Raw reset gate r of unit 6 (timing explains R^2 0.70: high at D2, low at GO). Beyond timing: at D1 (and less at GO) it is raised after an unrewarded a1 trial (+0.2 to 0.3, either state) and graded by the ideal observer belief that S1 is good (higher when S1 favoured). At D2 it depends on the transition just seen: a1 reaching S2 (rare) raises it about +0.2, a2 reaching S1 (rare) lowers it about -0.25, common transitions are near baseline. The free fit adds a separate drop at D1 after rewarded a2 trials and phase-specific belief weights at GO. Remaining misses: runs of unrewarded trials keep it high even after a2 choices, and it is over-predicted to drop after a2 S1 r. All terms observed; no future variables used.

issues: Most of the claims hold up. In the D1 residuals, a1 S1 u is +0.296 and a1 S2 u is +0.324, so the rise after unrewarded a1 does not depend on the state reached. The GO effect is weaker (+0.10 / +0.20). At D2, a1->S2 is +0.189, a2->S1 is -0.254, and the common transitions are about 0 (a1S1 -0.007, a2S2 +0.04). Dropping the reward condition (prev_action==1 only) lowers test to 0.54, so the 'unrewarded' part is needed. Restricting the a1-unrewarded term to D1 only lowers test to 0.61, which supports including GO.

The largest systematic miss contradicts the label's belief claim. The short form's misses show D1 after a2 S1 r over-predicted by -0.164. In the raw residuals, D1 after a2 S1 r is -0.185 and after a2 S2 r is -0.207. A rewarded a2 lowers the gate whichever state was reached, even when it pushes belief toward S1, which the label says should raise the gate. 'S1-favouring belief raises it' is therefore partly a stand-in for a choice-by-reward effect (a2 rewarded -> low). The explanation calls the a2-rewarded drop a free-fit-only extra, yet it is the biggest error class of the recorded short form.

Adding the a2-rewarded drop to the D1 belief term gives (phase == D1) * (np.tanh(belief_lo) - (prev_action == 2) * (prev_reward == 1)). This passes --short and raises test R^2 beyond timing from 0.659 to 0.702 (dev 0.714). It also shrinks the D1 a2 S1 r miss from -0.164 to -0.069. Other targeted variants did no better: belief at D1+GO 0.647, belief in all phases 0.583, sign(belief_lo) 0.647, (2*belief-1) 0.662, a2-rewarded as a separate third term instead of belief 0.605.

The label leaves out that the belief effect is D1-only and that the a1-unrewarded rise is at D1/GO. The D1 belief-decile profile looks more like a step at 0.5 (-0.18 to +0.19, with the jump between deciles 4 and 5) than a 'gradual' rise.

Errors that remain with either form: unrewarded runs carry over into D2 (D2 after a2 S2 u +0.10, after a1 S2 u +0.07 to +0.08), and GO after a1 S1 u is over-predicted (-0.09 to -0.10). These are moderate and do not overturn the overall picture. The observed-only additive ceiling is 0.86.
skeptic.revised_label: At D1/GO, rises after unrewarded a1; at D1, tracks S1-belief, drops after rewarded a2; at D2, signed rare transition.
